questions.question: What is TypeScript?
options: A new runtime that replaces Node.js
A JavaScript framework for user interfaces
JavaScript plus a static type checker
A language that compiles to WebAssembly
questions.explanation: TypeScript adds types and a checker to JavaScript; the output is ordinary JavaScript.

questions.question: What does "static" mean in "static type checker"?
options: Only static class members are checked
The code is checked without running it
The checker runs on a server
questions.explanation: Static analysis reads the code; dynamic checks happen while the program runs.

questions.question: Which statement is the "golden rule" of this book?
options: Annotations convert values to the declared type
TypeScript adds runtime validation for every function
Types are checked again at runtime
Types are erased: they never change what the JavaScript does at runtime
questions.explanation: tsc removes annotations; nothing about types survives into the emitted code.

questions.question: Which of these does TypeScript check for you? (select all that apply)
options: Calling a function with too few arguments
That JSON from an API has the right shape at runtime
Using a value that may be undefined
questions.explanation: TypeScript checks your code; runtime data must be validated by your code.

questions.question: In the error "app.ts(7,3): error TS2322: ...", what is (7,3)?
questions.explanation: tsc prints file(line,column) followed by the error code and message.

questions.question: What does TS2322 usually mean?
options: A type is not assignable to the expected type
A parameter implicitly has an any type
questions.explanation: TS2322 reads "Type X is not assignable to type Y".

questions.question: Why does `const pages = 412; pages.toUpperCase()` report the type 412 rather than number?
options: It is a bug in the compiler
A const gets the narrowest literal type, 412
Numbers are always shown as their value
questions.explanation: A const can never change, so TypeScript infers the literal type; let would give number.

questions.question: TypeScript compares object types by...
options: The file they are declared in
questions.explanation: If a value has the required properties, it fits the type, whatever it is called.

questions.question: What is the main change in TypeScript 7.0?
options: The compiler was ported to Go and runs about 10× faster
JavaScript files can no longer be compiled
Types are now checked at runtime
questions.explanation: TS 7 keeps the language rules of 6.0 and replaces the engine with a native one.

questions.question: Which statement about TypeScript 7 defaults is true?
questions.explanation: New in TS 7: strict mode is the default, so every example in the book uses it.

questions.question: Where can you try TypeScript in the browser without installing anything?
options: Nowhere: it needs a local install
questions.explanation: The Playground runs the compiler in the browser and shows errors and emitted JavaScript.

questions.question: Which ways of running TypeScript do NOT type-check? (select all that apply)
options: A bundler such as esbuild or Vite
questions.explanation: Only tsc checks types; the others strip them for speed. Run tsc --noEmit alongside.

questions.question: Is every JavaScript program also a TypeScript program?
options: No, you must add types first
Yes syntactically: it parses, though it may have type errors
questions.explanation: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript, which is why gradual migration works.

questions.question: Your team says "with TypeScript we can delete input validation". What is correct?
options: Validation is still needed at the edges; TS removes the need for internal shape checks
Validation must move into type annotations
TS only works if validation is removed
questions.explanation: Types are erased, so runtime input is unchecked; inside type-checked code, defensive checks become redundant.

questions.question: What does `x as any` do?
options: Throws if x is not valid
Converts x to any type at runtime
Switches off type checking for that value
questions.explanation: any disables checking; nothing happens at runtime.

questions.question: Which kinds of types does TypeScript add on top of JavaScript's own? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: bigint, string, number, boolean, symbol, null, undefined exist in JavaScript; any, unknown, never and void are TypeScript additions.

questions.question: How do Java/C# runtimes differ from TypeScript regarding types?
options: They keep type information at runtime; TypeScript erases all of it
questions.explanation: The JVM and .NET check casts at runtime; a failed TypeScript `as` never throws.

questions.question: Two separate jobs of tsc are...
questions.explanation: Checking and emitting are independent, which is why errors still emit.

questions.question: An object `{ title: "Dune", pages: 412 }` is passed to `shout(item: { title: string })`. Does it compile?
options: Yes: it has the required title
No: pages is an extra property
questions.explanation: A variable with extra properties fits; only fresh object literals get the excess property check.

questions.question: What are interfaces and type aliases used for?
questions.explanation: Both name types; they disappear after compilation.

questions.question: Which statement about TypeScript and runtime performance is true?
options: TypeScript adds runtime checks that cost time
Type annotations slow the program down
The emitted code runs at the same speed as equivalent hand-written JavaScript
questions.explanation: TS 7 made the compiler faster, not your program.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good reason to adopt TypeScript?
options: To validate API input automatically at runtime
questions.explanation: Runtime validation still needs code or a schema library.

questions.question: What does the editor use to show TypeScript errors as you type?
options: The same compiler, through the TypeScript language service
questions.explanation: Editor and tsc report the same errors when they use the same version.

options: TypeScript is JavaScript plus types: all runtime knowledge carries over

questions.explanation: The runtime semantics are exactly JavaScript's.
